supporting_observations.claim: During the alert window, WS-RDIAZ-01 (10.56.10.22) repeatedly established HTTP connections to the internal proxy at 10.56.20.30:8080. The records include sessions at 13:31:53, 13:40:54, 13:46:14, 13:50:46, 13:55:54, 14:01:05, 14:05:55, and 14:10:54 UTC.

Several of the recurring proxy connections have similar byte counts, including roughly 9.1–9.5 KB sent and 25.7–25.9 KB received. The available connection records do not identify the HTTPS destination or the originating application.
The recurring timing is compatible with a periodic check, but the available records do not establish that these sessions were made by the approved GradeBook Pro updater or that they were benign.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied collection status reports a log collection outage for WS-RDIAZ-01 winsec and sysmon from 13:30 to 14:15 UTC, preventing process-level attribution during the relevant period.
The supplied collection status reports a proxy-log collection outage from 13:30 to 14:15 UTC, so proxy records that could identify the HTTPS destinations are unavailable for most of the alert window.
The available Zeek connection records show connections to the internal proxy on port 8080, not the ultimate HTTPS destinations.
claims_not_established: Which domains or URLs the recurring sessions reached.
Which process initiated the sessions and whether it was the approved GradeBook Pro updater.
What content was exchanged, or whether any data was uploaded or downloaded.
Whether the alerted activity was malicious or benign.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy logs for 13:30–14:15 UTC, including CONNECT destinations, user agent, and request details.
Obtain endpoint process-to-network telemetry for WS-RDIAZ-01 during the alert window, including process paths, command lines, and parent processes.
Compare the recovered destinations and process activity with the approved GradeBook Pro updater and its expected update-check behavior.
unrelated_findings: After the alert window, raul.diaz accessed Google Drive, an unapproved cloud-storage service in the supplied environment context; route this separately and do not use it to determine the alert. Records: T265-00342, T265-00343, T265-00354.
